A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PolyNet and contain readable text, equations, tables, figures, and complete Appendices A–F. The method, experiments, and relocated material can be reliably matched.

before.justification: V1 reports original PolyNet experiments on TSP, CVRP, CVRPTW, and FFSP, including benchmark comparisons, ablations, and training and search analyses.

after.justification: V2 retains those empirical results and adds quantitative diversity measurements, strategy-contribution analyses, first-node statistics, and additional comparisons.

M1.justification: The bit-vector-conditioned decoder, residual layers, best-solution training objective, rollout-average baseline, free first-action selection, and EAS procedure are unchanged. The MatNet adaptation in Appendix A is also retained.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate the same routing problems at 100, 150, 200, and 300 nodes and FFSP instances with 20, 50, and 100 jobs. Data generators and represented problem conditions are unchanged; the new diagnostics use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: COMPASS, previously discussed but not tabulated, is added to the TSP and CVRP comparisons for 100 and 150 nodes in Tables 1–2. Appendix B also adds unmodified POMO to the layer-ablation comparison in v2 Figure 6. Other comparator memberships are retained.

E3.justification: V2 adds test-set aggregation of pairwise broken-pairs distances, counts each strategy's best-solution contributions across 10,000 instances, and measures distinct first-node selections. These introduce diagnostic evaluation procedures. Existing benchmark splits, training budgets, augmentation, and sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 substantially extends the central diversity investigation beyond training curves and selected-instance scatterplots. Section 4.3 adds aggregate diversity comparisons and tests whether all strategies contribute useful solutions and whether diversity extends beyond first-node selection. Appendix B adds a POMO control. Existing first-move, warm-start, and search-trajectory analyses remain.

E5.justification: Neither version provides confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Appendix E retains the explicit statement that its experiment, including training, was not replicated with multiple seeds. The added frequency distributions do not introduce uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: V2 adds substantive mechanism-level findings: Table 4 reports PolyNet/POMO diversity distances of 4.621/2.400, 18.535/16.785, and 19.969/18.162; Figures 4–5 show strategy contributions and mean distinct-first-node counts of 24.5, 3.8, and 7.0. COMPASS scores and POMO ablation curves are also added. Retained benchmark values in Tables 1–3 and the FFSP table match exactly. The first-move ablation drops absolute-objective entries while retaining gaps and runtimes.

T1.justification: The mathematical problem formulation, policy expression, training gradient, and baseline formula are unchanged, with no added proofs or theoretical results. V2's explanation of the standard broken-pairs distance clarifies an existing metric rather than introducing new mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: learning complementary strategies with one decoder, avoiding enforced first actions, and improving performance across four problems. The new diversity evidence supports these existing claims.

C2.justification: V2 explains how fewer distinct first nodes can still produce greater overall diversity and attributes frequent TSP strategy ties to near-optimal solutions. Appendix D qualifies v1's favorable diversity-versus-cost interpretation: diverse samples can cost more, but the objective is the best sampled solution. The scale and black-box limitations were already present.

D1.justification: V1 promises public release upon acceptance; v2 supplies a repository address and reports an implementation in RL4CO. This changes reported code access. Hardware, architecture dimensions, training hyperparameters, and Appendix F's instance-generation instructions are otherwise retained.

R1.justification: The literature review substantially expands research positioning, adding diversity in metaheuristics and discussion of constrained routing, heavy decoders, diffusion, and neural k-opt methods. New references include Mahfoud, Hanaka, Routefinder, and CAMP. V2 also introduces explicit critiques concerning prior methods' computational overhead, supervision requirements, and applicability.

P1.justification: The introduction and literature review undergo substantial rewriting. Search performance moves ahead of diversity, while separate training and search-diversity discussions become a unified, question-led Section 4.3. The scatterplot discussion moves into an expanded Appendix D, alongside smaller wording, affiliation, and cross-reference edits.

P2.justification: V2 reorganizes the diversity displays around a new summary table and two diagnostic figures. The redundant main-text scatterplot is removed while its examples remain in Appendix D. The layer-ablation plot gains a curve and revised legend, the first-move table loses objective columns and shares a row with the diversity table, and the decoder diagram is reduced with surrounding text.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens the diversity argument with aggregate measurements, strategy-contribution diagnostics, and direct COMPASS comparisons. Appendix D gives a more accurate account of the diversity–cost tradeoff, and reported code access improves reproducibility information. These are useful supporting refinements to an already substantial evaluation; the method and benchmark results remain unchanged, and uncertainty reporting is not strengthened.
